webpage.text:
Psst ...there's more to your favorite restaurant than you think

Don't be afriad to ask for something from the "secret menu."

There are secrets in this information-addicted world that, upon release, would catastrophically disrupt human society.

And then there are secrets of equal, if not more, importance that would improve the world as we know it today.

Don’t call me Edward Snowden, but what I am about to reveal to you will make you rethink your next few meals, even perhaps the rest of your life.

Ever wonder why there are only four options to choose from on the Chipotle menu? While many happy customers have their “usual” burrito or salad, don’t you ever feel like there could be something missing as you hand the cashier $6.25 and your soul? If not, ignorance is bliss, I guess.

But the thing you’ve been subconsciously searching for can be found on the “secret menu” at Chipotle. And Starbucks. And Panera. And so many more fast-food restaurants that will make you feel like you’ve been swindled all these years.

My first exposure to these classified menus occurred while I was indulging in some Mexican magic in the form of a Chipotle taco.

My friends had ordered what I thought was a normal burrito … but I was quickly corrected and introduced to a “quesarito”: a burrito with a quesadilla shell. It was love at first sight.

And just like that, my research of secret menus began.

An always-helpful friend named Google disclosed a website called hackthemenu.com. It revealed a entire list of fast-food restaurants with secret menus. However, the skeptic in me questioned some of the “secret” items listed for various restaurants.

Lucky for me, a friend who works at Panera was able to confirm there are, indeed, secret items Panera prepares. At this particular restaurant, only card members get notifications regarding these hidden treasures. (But I guess nothing stays under wraps for long!)

Panera offers “Power Salads” — these are one of the few offerings that don’t include bread, resulting in less carbs and more meals for health-conscious freaks who don’t want bread when they go to Panera Bread. (Seriously, you can’t live life in a green and leafy cocoon. Sorry, no offense, but it’s true.)

If you think you’ve enjoyed a great feast after downing a Big Mac at McDonald's, why not one-up yourself with a Monster Mac? Eight patties on one sandwich will bring new meaning to the definition of a “filling” meal.

Craving diversity? Try the Land, Sea and Air Burger — a Big Mac, Filet-O-Fish and McChicken all in one. (I will reserve comment here.)

Taco Bell’s secret menu offers a twist on a classic: substitute nacho cheese for creamy guacamole on your five-layer burrito. If you have a mouth with steel-like endurance for spicy flavoring, and the “fire” sauce just doesn’t have enough kick, ask for “lava” sauce … which you can order on basically anything on the menu (warning: may cause mouth fire).

I’m not even sure I should mention this next secret menu for the sake of the sanity of many poor baristas, but I feel it’s my duty to my fellow teenage girls to share. Yes, the hated-by-some, beloved-by-most Starbucks has a secret menu (please, just finish the article first before grabbing your keys …).

Much to my surprise (sarcasm!), there is a separate website for the green logo drinks that is simply starbuckssecretmenu.net that separates it into secret drinks by types and sizes. My personal favorites include the Willy Wonka Frap, Banana Foster Frap and the Swirl Pow Hot Chocolate.

While some of these restaurant employees may not know about the secret menus, if you politely explain the recipe to them, they are usually accommodating.

So now you know. My only hope is you use this information to better yourself, your appetite and the world.

As for this writer, well, as Edward Snowden said, “there’s no saving me.”
